sense.text:
“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. The Bible gives us the defense against the things Satan uses to destroy us, and the first defense is to pay attention.

We read “roaring lion” and think we will see him coming, that he will come at us loud and we will know it. No. Satan’s kiss comes as a gift. It comes as an opportunity. Satan uses his devices to appear good, to appear righteous, and it ends up being evil. Within our lust we pursue those things, because sin feels good: evil is good, as the vampire said.

Sin rarely presents itself as destruction. It presents itself as opportunity, pleasure, love, comfort, success, escape and validation. All those things sound great, and that is why you have to be in the spirit and in the scriptures to discern whether a thing is righteousness or Satan’s kiss to your demise.

“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation”, because everything in the world right now is against the person trying to be righteous. Everything is set up to keep us in the midst of sin and wickedness: the way your work schedule is set up so you are in the midst of sin on the weekend, your off time, the holidays you want off, all based off wickedness. So you have to be around righteous people who will hold you accountable.

“for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life”: you are going to be tried. The crown is “promised to them that love him.”

“Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man”. God is not tempting you. It is your own lust within you that is tempting you, and Satan using his devices on that lust.

“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed means there is an attraction there, something in us that makes us gravitate toward the things that cause us to sin. It seduces us. It looks like it is right for us, and it is not, and the only way to tell whether it is good for you is to filter it through the scriptures.

Temptation begins internally. The lust is in you, so when the temptation presents itself you are drawn to it. Sin starts enticing you, and it grows through agreement: you get enticed by it and you agree with it.

“Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin”: that attraction you agreed with becomes sin. “and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” Sin is the action you take after you have been enticed by your lust, and it always ends in destruction. That is why we have to be on point, because we think things in our mind are right and we are far off.

precepts.why:
“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” If you come to serve the Lord you are going to be tempted by Satan, and he is going to use devices to tempt you. That is why the man that endureth temptation is blessed: he is going to be tried.

“Set thy heart aright”: get your damn mind right, because this is not going to be a fair fight and it is not going to be easy. “and constantly endure”: you have demons in you that need purging, and some of these things will keep coming back, so you have to be able to fight them off. Paul was like that, asking the Lord to take it away from him, and it was the thorn in his side he had to battle. But that battle is also what keeps us going in this truth: always trying to get better with ourselves, in how we communicate, in our relationships, in how we deal with one another.

“make not haste in time of trouble”: things are going to happen and you cannot fold. Life is a fight, and everybody is not going to make it. “Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.”

“For gold is tried in the fire”. You are going to be tried, period, so make sure you are on point. That is the trying of James 1:12, and the crown of life is for the one who endures it.

“Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits”. That is the enticing of James 1:14. A seducing spirit looks like it is good for you, and it is going to destroy you, like crack to a crackhead: it feels real good, but he cannot see that his whole life is being destroyed around him.

That is why it is important to be studying, reading your four chapters, and being around godly men and godly women, so somebody has your back.

“There is a way which seemeth right unto a man”: in our mind we think it is the right thing. This sounds good, this sounds real good. “but the end thereof are the ways of death.” At the end is death and destruction, the same end as sin “when it is finished”.

When you have no discernment of what is going on and you counsel with yourself, you are going to be 100% right every time.

“Extol not thyself in the counsel of thine own heart”. Don’t big up your own counsel. In your mind you are always going to think you are 100% right, and that is why you have to get counsel.

A lot of you hate counsel, or you appear to want it: you sit down and do all the things you are supposed to do in counsel, but in your mind you have already made it up, and nobody can tell you what to do. Don’t mess with that brother, he is not ready; and you deal with him anyway, lay with him, marry him, and then the person is crazy and you want leadership to fix the mistake we told you not to make.

The job of leadership is to reason with the scriptures and give you scriptural advice, from the scriptures and experience, on how to maneuver in your situation. It is not to make the decision for you. Applying it is your decision, and that is on you. Your feelings are not a spiritual guide. Your thoughts, your emotion, your intuition will destroy you. Like Bishop always says, I don’t listen to myself. You have to be in the word.

“The heart is deceitful above all things”: your mind will deceive you, so that you think what you are thinking is right, the same way James shows a man drawn away of his own lust. I know me, they don’t understand me, I know what I’ve been through. “and desperately wicked”: that is why 1 Peter 5:8 says be on the lookout. “who can know it?” You don’t even know it. When you don’t get counsel you cannot see the danger zones you walk into by digging for yourself.

“I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.” Read on: “As the partridge sitteth on eggs, and hatcheth them not; so he that getteth riches, and not by right, shall leave them in the midst of his days, and at his end shall be a fool.”

Back in verse 6: “he shall be like the heath in the desert, and shall not see when good cometh; but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness”. Then verse 7: “Blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord”. That is the man that gets counsel, that reads the Bible and applies the commandments. The Lord set up men to guide us, and Black people hate guidance. That is low self-esteem: they see you and see themselves in you, and think, I’m nothing so he ain’t nothing, and that goes all the way back to what was done to us in slavery.

“Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.” Lust is not just temptation. It is an appetite. That lust is a buildup, and it becomes an appetite that sometimes feels impossible to fill: it wants more and more, and it multiplies and transfers into other things. A sexual appetite goes to gambling, and that might go to bestiality. You can never get enough if you don’t check it, and the Most High demands restraint. Don’t indulge in it.

“If thou givest thy soul the desires that please her, she will make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies that malign thee.” A lot of people do the sin, get put out, come back, and think everybody is looking at them and their sin. Nobody cares what you did; that was a long time ago. You still have that guilt and have not forgiven yourself, and Satan has your mind messed up so you think everybody is thinking something evil about you. See how Satan puts things in your head, based off the things you deal with.

“Turn away from me vain hopes and concupiscence”. Concupiscence is an intense, powerful desire. That is dangerous.

Like the man in the video, in a public place, who bent down like he was tying his shoe and licked a woman’s booty cheek while she was not even paying him any mind. That man has a demon on him. He could not control himself. A man who cannot control himself in public like that will rape, will kill, will do all manner of wickedness, because he cannot control that lust; the appetite is so strong. He walked up and tried to touch her immediately. He did not look around. He did not care about consequences, jail time or the camera, and he does that often, because something is overtaking his spirit. And that is a lot of you with porn, and you out at work or at Walmart, talking to women to see if you still got it, enticing that spirit. That is an appetite that cannot be filled.

What that man does openly was most likely done to him behind closed doors since he was a little boy. Those spirits do not pop up out of nowhere; it was built inside of him. That is why you have to watch your kids and really be able to trust the people around them, the nasty uncles and aunts, no matter how righteous they appear.

“and thou shalt hold him up that is desirous always to serve thee.” Turn me away from these strong desires, Lord; I don’t need them. “Let not the greediness of the belly nor lust of the flesh take hold of me”: don’t let my lustful appetite, what is inside of me, overtake me and destroy me, because that lust comes from Satan, and if it is not checked I am going to be tempted by it. “and give not over me thy servant into an impudent mind. Hear, O ye children, the discipline of the mouth: he that keepeth it shall never be taken in his lips.”

So we have to be scripturally mature to handle these situations. Like Deacon Ethan said, Satan comes in secrecy when you are by yourself. At the Sabbath you are cool, because everybody is watching. But some of you still go to the bathroom and watch your porn, sisters too, and it is going to come out. When you leave here, that appetite inside you starts to mess with your mind, because you are not around people who will hold you accountable.

“Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.” Do not let sin control you or have dominion over you. “Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God”. The body and the life God gave us are instruments to serve God. Your life is not your own; you cannot just do what you want with the body. It is supposed to be a temple, a holy thing.

Then verse 16: “Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” Whatever you decide to obey, you become its servant, and as long as you are serving sin you are serving sin unto death. That is the road you are going down, the death of James 1:15.

Christ was teaching about prayer, because of how bad the enemy is going to be treating us: “I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?”

It is going to get worse. That man in the video was so bold, and it is going to get to the point where people just start grabbing people. Sin is going to be so rampant in the earth, taking over people, and the demons so far out, especially in the Christian church, like the gay pastor saying Christ did not teach the law, when the same chapter speaks of adultery and the law.

That is why we are here pushing the laws and the faith of Christ: that is what will get us through. Without the law and that faith, you are not going to make it. That is also why sisters should not go to the gym or the store alone late at night, but go with a crowd, with other sisters, because there is a lot of evil out there.

“For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.” Some people around you will seem good and be evil as hell, with no good intentions for you. A lot of these pastors say they are apostles of Christ and they are a damn demon: infidelity, sex with young boys, impregnating young girls, embezzlement, taking your money. The people you hold in high regard are often the biggest phonies.

“And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.” Satan is not going to appear to you as evil, because you would see it. He comes to you as good opportunity, as things that seem good, as what you think is a healthy relationship, harmless fun, just business, just a friendship, and it is all wrapped up in evil. That is how a man is enticed.

It is not just the pastors. It is your auntie, your mama, your daddy, big mama who cooked the good food and raised you, who can do no wrong, and is a demon in reality. That is why you have problems in the truth letting go of people who harm you spiritually.

sense.text:
What ultimately messed us all up was the woman. Sisters, you have to bear that burden. But we love you, and the righteous sisters in IUIC are the cream of the crop, getting yourselves together.

“Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field”. “Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” The woman answered that of “the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.” This fruit is idolatry. We are a spiritual people, and throughout history we always try to find something to believe in, instead of what we are supposed to believe in: keeping the commandments and having faith in the Lord and his son, Jesus the Christ. Same way in Egypt, same way now in America. Everything seems better on the other side; we live in a grass-is-greener society. There are no fruits in Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, Judaism or any of this religion. It looks good and sounds good, but read the Bible as it is written and people get offended and will try to kill you. We have done everything for 400 years except keep the commandments.

“And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die”. Satan enticed this woman: nothing is going to happen to you, what I am presenting to you is good. “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.”

A lot of women are gullible because they don’t want to listen and think they know it all. The woman was created to help, supplemental to the man; where we lack, you come in. We are not asking you to think; we do the thinking. That is why the father has the power to take away your vow, and the husband has the same power: we are the progenitors of leadership, structure and order. We just need you to follow, and when you think too much and think you know more, you fall into sin and wickedness.

“And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise”: she saw it. She was visibly attracted to that doctrine, that idolatry, and enticed by it. “she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat”: she thought it might be good for her. “and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat”: he indulged in the idolatry too.

See the power of the woman to manipulate and convince a man into utter wickedness. The other side of it: a spiritual woman is the last line of defense to save that man, to speak sense into him. That is where the help meet comes in: I don’t agree with that, honey, I think you’re looking at it wrong, take some time. But instead the pillow talk gets to you.

The pattern of sin is attraction, then justification, it’s just one time, it ain’t going to hurt nobody, then action, then the consequence. All bread is sweet to a whoremonger, and he does not count losing his marriage, splitting his family, seeing his children once a month, and losing half in the process.

precepts.why:
“Such things they did imagine, and were deceived: for their own wickedness hath blinded them.” What you have in your mind deceives you, and you think you are right. Their own wickedness can be read as their own appetite, their own lust, their own desires: it blinds them so they cannot see anything else. That man in the public place was blinded by his lust, and he is not the only one.

“As for the mysteries of God, they knew them not”: they were not in the scriptures. “neither hoped they for the wages of righteousness”. The wages of sin is death, so the wages of righteousness is life, and you did not consider that when your mind was messed up. You did not count the cost. “nor discerned a reward for blameless souls.”

“For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.” Think how important we are: we were supposed to be here forever, created in his image. “Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world”. Through the devil, through that appetite and lust, came death, which is sin. That happened in Genesis, and that is why we die today. The serpent said “Ye shall not surely die”, and death is exactly what came.

“and they that do hold of his side do find it.” Sin blinds judgment. Most of the problems in your life are dumb decisions you made. The Most High gives you his spirit so you can discern and prosper, but once desire leads, reasoning follows desire.

sense.text:
“My son, keep my words, and lay up my commandments with thee. Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye. Bind them upon thy fingers, write them upon the table of thine heart. Say unto wisdom, Thou art my sister; and call understanding thy kinswoman”. Keep the commandments close, like a sister, like a kinswoman.

This hits home with problems in your marriages. Men, it is up to you to fix the problems in your marriage. Sometimes the wife is the devil, but not always; sometimes you are the problem, and your wife has been trying to speak on it while you keep it on the low to keep doing your evil. It is not leadership’s job to fix your marriage. Use the scripture to fix it.

“That they may keep thee from the strange woman”: that is where it starts. Keep the commandments close so they keep you from the strange woman, unpredictable, you don’t know what to expect. “from the stranger which flattereth with her words.” You get no words of affirmation from your wife, she doesn’t rub on you or love on you, and the first woman out and about who compliments you, you are done: I still got it. That demon knows exactly what you are lacking, the words and triggers that set off your lust.

“For at the window of my house I looked through my casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding”. Void of understanding: he does not see the signs. He is spiritually young and cannot discern.

“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” Dressed like a whore, with everything you like popping out at every angle, and deceit behind it. Subtle of heart is someone cunning, deceitful, harboring hidden motives under a gentle exterior: trickery, manipulation. Satan knows what you desire and puts it in front of you. That is a temptation, and you have an avenue to move away from it. “She is loud and stubborn; her feet abide not in her house”.

“I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved works, with fine linen of Egypt.” This is a man who has already failed the decision; he is in the house. Decisions have to be made on a dime, and the Lord gives you clues, that little spiritual voice saying I shouldn’t be doing this. That is the Lord telling you.

The silk sheets, “I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon”: she smells good, she looks good, and it is destruction. “Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning”. You are living in a sexless marriage, and this woman comes and says let’s go all night. She talks to him, cooks him a good meal; he feels like he can conquer the world when he talks to her.

“Hearken unto me now therefore, O ye children, and attend to the words of my mouth. Let not thine heart decline to her ways, go not astray in her paths.” Keep the commandments and keep it simple; don’t let Satan use the appetite in you to fill that hunger.

“For she hath cast down many wounded”: a lot of men and women are wounded ducks. They have been down so long that everything that appears good is good to them. They are weak, and that is when Satan comes in. “yea, many strong men have been slain”.

The cleanup woman is real. A cousin’s husband worked at a jail, came home to a dirty house, no food, the laundry not done, and a wife who was a demon to him; a woman at his job brought him lunch and washed his clothes, and she took a married man, and he left his family. She was smooth, and he could not see he was about to lose his family. Sisters, with a sexless marriage, not desiring your husband, a filthy house and no food, you put the thought and desire in him to want more.

precepts.why:
“Yea, many there be that have run out of their wits for women”. Many men have run out of their wits for women, and the other way too. A lot of sisters are sitting ducks: we told you, he ain’t right, but he is tall, dark and handsome, and when you lie down with him and it doesn’t go the way you wanted, it is not on us to fix your marriage. You made him your lord; we cannot come and dictate his house. Our job is to use the scriptures to give wise counsel.

Read back for the context, where they were trying to find what the strongest thing is: “Then the third, who had spoken of women, and of the truth, (this was Zorobabel)”. “O ye men, it is not the great king, nor the multitude of men, neither is it wine, that excelleth; who is it then that ruleth them, or hath the lordship over them? are they not women?”

“and become servants for their sakes. Many also have perished, have erred, and sinned, for women.” Men have died behind the woman. A brother whose wife jumped out of a moving car would not leave her, because it was so good. You can be enticed so that you will go through years of demise and despair. Everything in America is dictated by the woman: men will kill and rob to get the attention of women, and the clothes, the jewels, the car and the money are all to entice a woman. A man is enticed by a woman who speaks smoothly and creates emotional comfort.

“Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent”. You have to get away from that thing. You don’t negotiate with temptation; you flee immediately. If it seems wrong, get away from it, and it does not take long to think about it: if you have any doubt about the judgment you are about to make, leave it alone, because something isn’t right.

Satan does not force sin. He suggests it, wraps it up in something else, beautifies it and rationalizes it, but ultimately you have to agree with it. Don’t let Satan give you that kiss on the cheek.

This is not justifying the man stepping out. This is how you defend your home, and Paul says the same thing. “Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence”: due benevolence is sex. The scripture says give him sex. “and likewise also the wife unto the husband. The wife hath not power of her own body, but the husband: and likewise also the husband hath not power of his own body, but the wife.”

It is mostly toward the women, but there are men too who are not giving anything in the bedroom, and the sisters are getting themselves together and get nothing. You create that demon, and the next thing you know a work husband comes into place. It brings other levels of sin, and that sin can go anywhere.

sense.text:
Samson’s downfall. “And it came to pass afterward, that he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah. And the lords of the Philistines came up unto her, and said unto her, Entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth”. It was a setup the whole time. Entice him, because he loves you: big burly men and a little dainty woman, and they just love that woman, and you can get enticed easily with good words.

“that we may bind him to afflict him: and we will give thee every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver.” Men telling a woman to go in and entice this man. In his mind he loves her and can trust her, and he is being played. Satan will use certain people to come in and manipulate you. Don’t let anybody manipulate you; be mindful of the wiles of the devil.

“And Delilah said to Samson, Tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth, and wherewith thou mightest be bound to afflict thee.” Why do you need to know that? That is a setup, and he was so gone he was not paying attention. Samson gave in, she cut his locks while he slept, and it was a done deal.

Women can manipulate and get you to do things if you are not spiritually sound, the way women today throw water on their men, cut off their hair, or throw away the PlayStation for TikTok views. Samson’s downfall was compromise, emotional attachment and physical attraction; he ignored all the warning signs, and that is what gets us caught up.

precepts.why:
“Turn away thine eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another’s beauty”. Don’t look at her lustfully because she looks good, because things start going into your mind. “for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman”, like 1 Esdras 4 said, many have erred for women.

Some women are fine, with the body, all dainty, and are a full-fledged demon. The Bible is telling you to beware; this is not made up. The Lord knows what he created and what is powerful. The box is powerful. Some of you brothers are weak; don’t be deceived by it.

sense.text: “And it came to pass in an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king’s house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.” He went out and saw a woman washing herself, bad to the bone, like Bishop says.

“And David sent and enquired after the woman.” He was attracted and had power, so he sent people to make it official. “And one said, Is not this Bath–sheba”, “the wife of Uriah the Hittite?” Someone there had spirit enough to make it plain: this is somebody’s wife, what is wrong with you?

“And David sent messengers, and took her”: he sent them anyway. “and she came in unto him, and he lay with her”. She was not right either. She did not resist; she thought she came up. See how easy it was: no resistance. “for she was purified from her uncleanness: and she returned unto her house.”

“And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.” That sounds like today: you get that call. Satan put that lust in him so that he did not care. Later he put Uriah in battle and got him killed and took his wife. People be plotting. What he saw, his desire, the action, the cover-up, the putting to death, and the consequences: his first child was gone.

precepts.why:
“And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David.” So we know who is being spoken of. “As is the fat taken away from the peace offering”.

Then: “The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” The Lord forgave David. He loved David, and David repented of all of it.

We are going to fall and do things that are not comely according to the scriptures. That does not mean you go into a fetal position and say woe is me. You get yourself together, repent, and move forward, and don’t go back. Christ said go and sin no more. We all make mistakes; it is how you handle the mistake. What are you going to do now, moving forward?

sense.text:
“Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests, And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you?” Some of you have partners like this, brothers in the truth and in other camps willing to lie, steal and cheat for money. A whole Israelite camp broke up back in the day over money. Now the lesser ones are pushed on every platform as the face of the Israelites, not the bishops and deacons really out in the streets teaching the word, and money is involved; the powers that be are pushing those interviews. This is war. The Black Panther Party, Martin Luther King, Malcolm X: people will give you up for money. If you are weak in spirit, money brings betrayal.

Judas walked with Christ. He healed people and kept the commandments, but that money lust is never enough. He desired riches more than anything. “And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.”
“And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him.” Judas betrayed the Lord Jesus Christ. He chased money and destroyed himself; money was his demise.

precepts.why:
“He that loveth gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof. Gold hath been the ruin of many”. Sometimes money is your ruin. You don’t make sound decisions and you are willing to do anything for it, like young women on OnlyFans and podcasts, willing to be abused in another country for money, then going home to kiss their kids. What morals do you have? It may look good because of the opportunity, but all things are not good.

“and their destruction was present. It is a stumblingblock unto them that sacrifice unto it”. It is a sacrifice: it is all you think about and talk about, your existence is based off money. That means it is your god, and that is why you sacrifice to it. “and every fool shall be taken therewith.”

“Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish”, because it is hard to have riches and keep the commandments: there are so many ways to be enticed when you can do and buy whatever you want, and some feel they are above everybody. Without blemish, you use your money properly and it doesn’t mess with your head. “and hath not gone after gold”: you have a lot of money but you have not made it your god.

“Seek not death in the error of your life: and pull not upon yourselves destruction with the works of your hands.” When you put that sin above everything, you are seeking death. Money can be your destruction. Women can be your destruction. Food, alcohol, drugs can be your destruction. That is the appetite in us that we constantly want to feed, and we have to stop it.

sense.text: This is how you are supposed to do it, when your back is against the wall. “And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man”. “his master saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hand.” Joseph had everything right; everything was in his favor. He was promoted overseer over the house, to oversee what comes in and goes out and give account. “the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake”. “And Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured.”

“his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.” Satan had to come in: it is too good in here, you have been promoted, the Lord is with you, so I have to test you and see if you really are a goodly man. She did not just say hello; she offered herself, and she was surely dressed to appeal, attractive and smelling good. The women back then were good to the eye.

“But he refused”: no, I’m good, this is not right, this man trusted me to oversee his house. If he had been weak in the spirit it would have happened. “neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife”: you are off limits.

Joseph reasoned it through: the Lord gave me favor and put me over everything in this house. “how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” That is adultery, fornication. He immediately resisted the devil: an easy decision, no negotiation, no emotional engagement. She was not ugly: she was the king’s wife, and he had the pick of the litter and chose her. Joseph did not care how fine she was. That he went straight to the law shows the scripture was always in his mind, in the frontal lobe of his brain.

Eve engaged and rationalized; Samson compromised and lost his strength; David looked and acted and lost a son; Judas chased money and destroyed himself; Joseph fled immediately and the Lord promoted him with blessings. Sometimes you pray, Lord take this away from me, and immediately you are put in a situation to prove yourself, and you fail because you did not recognize what was going on.

Today’s traps: sexual sin, thirst traps. “Flee fornication.” Flee it. Get away from it. “Every sin that a man doeth is without the body; but he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body.” Once you go outside of Christ you are sinning against your own self. You put yourself in that predicament.

precepts.why: “Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids. For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread”. A lot of us are weak to the woman, weak to the box. Those eyelashes are there for a reason, fluttering at you all dainty; in the old cartoons, in the love scene, the eyelashes grow. Don’t let it take you over. “and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.”

sense.text: Pornography and private sin. “whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” A lot of brothers and sisters do that: you are scrolling, something catches your eye, and next thing you know you are going down the rabbit hole, full-fledged, not caring about consequences, convinced in your sin.

precepts.why:
This is how you fix it. “I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?” You have to control what you view and what you desire. Seeing a beautiful woman does not mean you should think lustfully about that sister. Married men especially should have a covenant with their eyes with their wife.

“For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high? Is not destruction to the wicked?”

sense.text:
Addiction. “There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able”. The Lord still gives you enough strength not to be overtaken by these temptations; he always gives you a way out. “but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” It is up to you. We are weak in the faith and the spirit when we don’t read four chapters a day, our conversation is not about the scriptures, and we are not around the brothers, and Satan gets hold of us.

Temptation always comes with an exit. Addiction forms when we stop taking the exit.

“Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry.” Idolatry is so important in speaking of temptation because you idolize these temptations. That appetite, the lust within you, is an idol to you. You idolize the demon inside of you, you feed it, and it is never enough.

precepts.why:
When we don’t study, we have nothing in our spirits to combat Satan, and we are defenseless. Even Christ, when he was tempted, used the word of God: it is written.

“Blessed is the man that doth meditate good things in wisdom, and that reasoneth of holy things by his understanding.” We saw it with Joseph. When you are in a compromising situation you have to have something up there to combat that lust: when you meditate on good things you can reason in the scriptures, the scripture says this, I can’t do that. “He that considereth her ways in his heart”: always ask, what does the scripture say about this?

Bishop made the point that when you go before the magistrates you think not what you are going to say, but you have to have something in your spirit for the Lord to work with. If you have no scriptures about lust in your head, where will you pull from? Give the Holy Spirit something to work with. Studying is heavy. When Joseph was tempted he referred back to the law, sin against God: that came to his mind first.

“Let not the greediness of the belly nor lust of the flesh take hold of me; and give not over me thy servant into an impudent mind.” This is what we must do when we pray and make supplication to the Lord: please take this away from me. We know what we deal with, and we have to be honest with ourselves and with the Lord about what we want him to take away.

Sin feels good to everybody, and some don’t care and bask in the evil. But when you have done wrong, you should feel like the worst servant ever: Lord, take this away from me. That is what you should feel like.

sense.text: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” You think you know it all, that you have all the wisdom and understanding. Pride is the progenitor of your destruction, because pride removes correction: you don’t want to hear it. Pride isolates you, and pride precedes the collapse.

precepts.why:
“The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That means you have a froward mind.

“For pride is the beginning of sin”, because you knew better. You had the warning signs, the opportunity, everything placed in front of you, and a way to escape, as 1 Corinthians 10 says. But pride overcame you; your mind was not on the Lord when your back was against the wall. Pride is the beginning of falling to sin, to temptation, to your lust, to feeding that appetite. “and he that hath it shall pour out abomination”: a prideful man is unstoppable.

“and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities”. When pride overtakes you, the Lord adds to your demise and leaves you to Satan to gobble you up, because your mind is not right.

“For froward thoughts separate from God”. Being froward means you are thinking outside of the Bible, period. When your mind is not on the Lord, you are separated from him; you cannot be both. That is the departing from God that is the beginning of pride.

This is how much the Lord hates a proud man. “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.” The Lord loves those things. It is hard for two personalities to come together on the same accord, which is why marriage takes time, years and experience.

Then the negative: “Three sorts of men my soul hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer”. A man that is poor and proud: I hate his soul, I hate everything about him. He has no humility; nobody can tell him anything. He has all the answers and no fruits in his life, no solutions, no shame.

sense.text:
Money. “For the love of money is the root of all evil”. People love what comes with money: attraction, power, respect, desirability. That is what people desire in America, rather than to be known as a righteous, loyal brother who gives good and wise counsel from the scriptures. Money is the root because it brings all those elements you deal with to the surface. Brothers wear the jewelry for attention, to entice a woman, and will rob their own people to have it.

“which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith”. A lot of women in marriages covet other people’s marriages by what they have: a big house, a new car, the trips. You feel your marriage is inadequate, not knowing they struggled for 10, 15, 20 years before anything was established, and you don’t know what goes on behind closed doors. You are married to another man in your heart, desiring what he does in his house. That is breaking the commandment: thou shalt not covet.

precepts.why:
You are looking at what that brother is doing and you are mad at your husband because he is not doing the same, and he is probably trying to get where he needs to be. But “Every wise woman buildeth her house”. You don’t know what she is doing for him to act like that. Why aren’t you studying her? Ask her how she builds up her house.

The wise woman has a mind for what is going on in the house: these are the things I need to fix, how I assist my husband. That is why Genesis says her desire shall be to her husband: you study him, his likes, his dislikes, when to leave him alone and when to speak. Your pride, sister, keeps you from doing it, thinking he has to give you everything first before you do your part as a wife. He is out providing, feeding, clothing the children, paying the bills. “but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands”: you might be the reason your marriage is the way it is.

In the marriage-counsel scene, Satan walked in and put his hand on the woman first, and she started speaking before the man said a word: who did Satan go to first? The woman. The white woman saw the demon, the trail of slime like a snail; the new priest could not see it, because he battles lust himself and cannot discern in the spirit. Some of you who counsel are not fit to counsel yet; you don’t have the experience to see the demon in there. Satan walks right into our marriages, hands on the shoulders of both, sitting on the couch stirring everything up, and nobody sees it. Who invited him? You did, when you did not study, did not do what God said, and did not listen to the leaders. Those who counsel have to find where the error is, not just side with whoever came first crying; sometimes the brother who looks righteous here is a tyrant at home.

sense.text:
Social media and the validation people want from it. “The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe.” Social media is a trap, a snare, a device Satan uses to keep our minds off the Lord. It is not just the children; it is us as adults, taking time from studying, from conversations with your wife, from setting marriage goals, from your children. All day it is ass shaking, and the more you consume it the more desensitized you are to the evil in the world. The children cry when they cannot get on the tablet; it is a fixation.

Everything you search and look at is tracked, and the algorithm is built to use your psychology against you: you think it just popped up, but they know how you think. And what does it all go back to? Sex, money, power: sin. Your social media is out to destroy you, not to make things convenient.

The work husband, the work deception. It happens where there is a sexless marriage or a spouse not doing what the other wants, leaving a void. Brothers in the warehouses, at Amazon, be careful: the young girls are predators and know when you are not happy at home, and the men know when the women are unhappy. In the body too, work husbands and work wives in the same office. It starts with you smell good today, the seed is planted, the compliments get bolder, the talks longer, then texting, and you justify it: they understand me, they listen more than my spouse, it is just harmless joking. Frequent conversation, emotional comfort, private communication, keeping a secret, complaining about your spouse to somebody else, emotional dependency: that is evil. Like Satan as an angel of light, it looks like a diligent coworker who cares so much.

“Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?” You are going to get burned; put fire that close and it will consume you. “Can one go upon hot coals, and his feet not be burned? So he that goeth in to his neighbour’s wife; whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.” The Bible has everything in it to fix our people, but when you are not in it, the Bible becomes your enemy, because it tells you the truth.
“Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.” When you put in the sin, the consequences are going to happen, period.

“For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption”: sow that sin to your flesh and you will be judged by it. “but he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.” When you sow yourself in the scriptures, the Lord gives blessings, favor, mercy and abundance.

precepts.why: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night”. We should meditate on the scriptures day and night, “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous”. When we put our mind on the Lord, he makes our way prosperous and gives us the increase we desire, spiritually, emotionally, in all things. That is sowing to the Spirit.
“For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” What you put in, you are going to get. You are going to receive a reward.

“I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live”. Life and death are both set before you; what you sow is your choice.

“And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve”. You cannot serve two masters. You cannot serve the flesh and God at the same time; you have to choose, and there is no in between. That is why he said he would rather you be cold or hot: if you are lukewarm, playing games in the middle ground, he will spew you out of his mouth.

“whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.”
